title: Yoghurt Parfait
subtitle: Layers of yoghurt, granola, and fresh berries
excerpt: A yoghurt parfait is an assembly job, yoghurt, crunchy granola, and fresh berries layered into a tall glass in the right order, which matters more than it sounds. The granola needs to go between layers of yoghurt, not piled on top, so it doesn't sog out immediately. Made this way it holds its crunch for up to an hour in the fridge.
sourceNotes: The layered yoghurt parfait is a modern British breakfast and brunch dish, adapted from the American parfait tradition. The word parfait comes from French, meaning 'perfect', and originally referred to a frozen cream dessert. The yoghurt-and-granola version became a café and hotel breakfast staple in the UK from the early 2000s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 1 hour ahead and refrigerate. Add the top granola layer just before serving.

content.text: A yoghurt parfait takes ten minutes and looks like more effort than it is. The key decision is the order: yoghurt first at the bottom, then {{granola}} granola, then berries, then another layer of yoghurt, more berries, and a small scatter of granola on top. Sandwiching the granola between layers of {{greek-yoghurt}} yoghurt stops it going entirely soft. The layer touching the yoghurt will soften, but layers further in stay crunchy. Tall glasses show the layers better than bowls do.
Hull and halve the {{strawberries}} strawberries. Put the {{blueberries}} blueberries in a small bowl alongside them.

Take two tall glasses, a 350 to 400 ml capacity is about right. Spoon 2 tablespoons of {{greek-yoghurt}} Greek yoghurt into the base of each glass and smooth it level. Add a tablespoon of {{granola}} granola, then a layer of mixed berries. Add another 2 to 3 tablespoons of yoghurt, smooth again, then more berries. Repeat until the glass is nearly full. Finish with a small handful of berries and a light scatter of {{granola}} granola. Drizzle with {{honey}} honey if you're using it.

Serve immediately, or refrigerate for up to 1 hour. Beyond that the granola softens through and loses its texture. If you want to make it further ahead, keep the components separate and assemble at the last moment.
For children, use a shorter, wider glass so the layers are visible without needing to peer down from above.
Use the maple pecan granola from this collection for a richer, more caramel-flavoured version.
In winter, swap fresh berries for a spoonful of berry compote, the warm fruit against cold yoghurt is a good combination.
Plain yoghurt works in place of Greek if that's what you have, though the parfait will be thinner and less rich.
A teaspoon of vanilla extract stirred through the yoghurt before layering adds a subtle sweetness that complements the berries.
